question: The tissue that stores fat is called:
solution:
The correct answer is __**adipose tissue**__ [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] **__Key Points__**

__
 
• The tissue that stores fat is called adipose tissue. Adipose tissue is a type of loose connective tissue that stores excess nutrients as fat.
 
• It's made up of fat cells called adipocytes, which contain lipid droplets of stored triglycerides. 
 
• Adipose tissue is found in several locations, including: Beneath the skin, Around internal organs, Between muscles, and Bone marrow. 
 
• Adipose tissue has several important functions, including:
 
• Storing and releasing energy: Adipose tissue stores energy and releases it to fuel the body. 
 
• Releasing hormones: Adipose tissue releases hormones that are important to the body's needs. 
 
• Protecting the body: Adipose tissue protects the visceral parts of the body. 
 
• Insulating and maintaining body temperature: Adipose tissue insulates and maintains the body temperature. 
 
• In mammals, there are two types of adipose tissue: white adipose tissue (WAT) and brown adipose tissue (BAT)

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

 
• Epithelial Tissue​

 
 
• A type of tissue that forms the covering or lining of all body surfaces, cavities, and hollow organs. It also makes up glands.
 
• Functions:
 
 
• Protection (e.g., skin).
 
• Absorption (e.g., intestinal lining).
 
• Secretion (e.g., glands).
 
• Filtration (e.g., kidney tubules)
 
 
 
 
 
• Connective Tissue
 
 
• A tissue that connects, supports, binds, or separates other tissues or organs.
 
• It is characterized by an abundance of extracellular matrix.
 
 
• Functions:
 
• Structural support (e.g., bones).
 
• Transport of nutrients (e.g., blood).
 
• Energy storage (e.g., adipose tissue).
 
• Immunological defense (e.g., lymph).
 
 
 
 
 
• Areolar Tissue
 
 
• A type of loose connective tissue that is widely distributed under the skin and around organs.
 
• Functions:
 
• Binds skin to underlying structures.
 
• Provides cushioning and support.
 
• Plays a role in immune defense by containing cells like macrophages and mast cells.
